# PV101 Day 4 Daily Run Sheet

Instructor-facing plan for Rich

CTS Cohort 6 - PV101 | Day 4 | Thursday, July 9, 2026

Topic: Small Solar System Build: PV Panel, Charge Controller, 12.8V LiFePO4 Battery, Wiring, and Inverter

Class setup: 6 students; 5 kits. 5 kits for 6 students: run 5 build stations. One station is a two-student team with Builder/Inspector roles that swap halfway. Solo builders still require a neighbor peer-check before energizing.

# Teaching frame

Main message: build the small solar system slowly enough that every part can be traced and explained.

The real lab is not just making the inverter turn on. The real lab is safe sequence, polarity, protection, and documentation.

5 kits for 6 students: run 5 build stations. One station is a two-student team with Builder/Inspector roles that swap halfway. Solo builders still require a neighbor peer-check before energizing.

Safety boundary: no energized wiring changes. Disconnect before touching conductors.

# Learning targets

Identify PV panel, charge controller, 12.8V LiFePO4 battery, inverter, protection, and conductors.

Wire a small solar system in the correct general sequence: battery/controller first, PV second, inverter battery-side through protection.

Use a multimeter to verify battery voltage, PV polarity/voltage, and controller-side readings before energizing.

Explain why the inverter is protected and why it is not treated like a tiny controller load.

Shutdown and document the system safely.

# Materials

5 small solar system kits for 6 students

Each kit: 1 PV panel, 1 charge controller, 1 12.8V LiFePO4 battery, 50Ah, 1 inverter, wiring/connectors, and required protection/disconnects

Multimeters with leads

Wire strippers

Ratcheting crimpers and correct dies

Appropriate ring terminals/lugs/ferrules/connectors

Inline fuse holders, fuses, or demo breakers sized for the training kit

Tape/labels/markers

Safety glasses

Panel covers, cardboard, towel, or face-down placement to keep PV inactive during wiring

Small approved AC test load if inverter testing is allowed

Student notebooks and measurement log sheets

# Daily schedule

| Time | Block | Instructor notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10:00-10:10 | Arrival + setup | Students get notebooks and quiz sheet. Instructor confirms kits remain disconnected: PV covered/unplugged, battery fuse out, inverter off. |
| 10:10-10:20 | Safety reset + goal | Frame the day: each group will build a small solar system, but nothing is energized until it is traced, metered, and approved. |
| 10:20-10:35 | Morning quiz | Individual, quiet. Use as a teaching check, not a trap. Humanity already invented enough traps, naturally. |
| 10:35-10:55 | Quiz review | Correct together. Tie missed answers back to today's physical build. |
| 10:55-11:20 | Slides part 1 | System pieces: PV panel, charge controller, LiFePO4 battery, inverter, fuses/disconnects, conductors. |
| 11:20-11:45 | Instructor demo | Show correct connection order: battery to controller first, then PV to controller, then inverter to battery side through protection. |
| 11:45-12:00 | Whiteboard challenge | Students trace the path: sunlight -> PV -> controller -> battery -> inverter -> AC load. Mark every positive and negative path. |
| 12:00-12:30 | Lunch / reset | All kits remain disconnected. Batteries stored safely. Panels covered or face-down. |
| 12:30-12:45 | Kit assignment + roles | Set 5 stations for 6 students. One pair shares a kit and swaps Builder/Inspector roles. Explain peer-check standard. |
| 12:45-1:05 | Mechanical prep | Students mount/lay out controller, battery, inverter, protection, and wires. Strip/crimp as needed. No power yet. |
| 1:05-1:35 | Build step 1: battery side | Wire battery to charge controller battery terminals through correct polarity. Fuse remains removed/open until approval. |
| 1:35-2:00 | Build step 2: PV side | Wire PV panel to charge controller PV input. Panel stays covered/disconnected until meter checks and instructor approval. |
| 2:00-2:20 | Build step 3: inverter side | Wire inverter to battery side through fuse/disconnect. Do not wire inverter output into anything permanent. Test only with approved small load. |
| 2:20-2:40 | Commissioning + measurements | Groups trace aloud, meter battery voltage (~12.8V nominal), verify PV polarity/voltage, then energize in approved order. |
| 2:40-2:55 | Cleanup + exit ticket | Disconnect PV first, turn inverter off, remove/open battery protection, document measurements, return kits. |
| 2:55-3:00 | Dismissal | Tools counted, scraps contained, batteries and panels safe. No mystery wires left behind, because we are not summoning demons. |

# Safety stop conditions

Polarity is uncertain or readings do not match expectation.

PV panel is producing voltage while students are still changing wiring.

Battery fuse blows, breaker trips, arc/spark appears, or equipment smells hot.

A conductor is warm, damaged, loose, or has exposed copper outside a terminal.

A student wants to change wiring while anything is energized.

Inverter wiring path is unclear or routed through the wrong controller terminals.

The group cannot explain the full energy path clearly.

# Whiteboard prompts

Where does energy enter the system?

Where is energy stored?

Where is energy converted to AC?

What gets connected first to most charge controllers?

Where should protection be placed so it protects the most conductor?

What measurement proves the system is ready for the next connection?

# Exit ticket

Trace the system path in words: PV panel -> charge controller -> battery -> inverter -> load.

What gets connected first on most charge controllers: battery or PV? Why?

Name one STOP condition from today's lab.
